subject: Burst capacity term sheet — surge rates, cooldowns, and commit trade-offs
messages:

Cc: Daniel Park <cto@acme-bio.com>

Subject: Clarification on burst pricing + cooldown for Dedicated GPU pool

Hi Rishi / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — Acme is excited about the dedicated GPU pool approach. Before we move to SOW/PO, procurement has a couple of open questions on the burst/autoscaling add-on:

- We need a clear definition of "surge rate" vs. "committed throughput" in the pricing sheet. Is surge invoiced per-token at a premium, or is it a flat per-minute charge?
- What's the typical cooldown window after a surge event? We're concerned about repeated short spikes and how they translate to cost.
- For a 12-month reserved commit, what discount bands do you offer if we add a burst add-on (e.g., 25% commit + burst vs. 50% commit)?

Can you send a concise term sheet showing three pricing scenarios (low/med/high burst usage) and how the cooldown behaves? We also attached the commit summary for the workloads we discussed.

Appreciate it — Laura

Attachment: ACME-requested-commit-summary.xlsx

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarification on burst pricing + cooldown for Dedicated GPU pool

Hi Laura / Daniel — thanks for the clear ask and for the commit spreadsheet. High level answers below, then I attached a short term sheet and an addendum draft. Will follow up with a quick call if you prefer.

1) Surge rate vs committed throughput
- Committed throughput = the guaranteed tokens/sec we reserve on your Dedicated pool. Priced as part of the monthly reserved commit (flat monthly fee tied to GPU count and target qps).
- Surge (burst) = temporary capacity above the committed level. We price surge usage in two components: a per-token premium when consuming KV/batch-sensitive resources, plus a per-minute activation fee for very short bursts (under 3 minutes) to cover scheduling overhead. The attached term sheet shows examples.

2) Cooldown behavior
- Default cooldown = 15 minutes after a sustained surge (sustained = >3 minutes). During cooldown, further surge activations are billed at the higher surge-per-token premium (no additional activation fee). We can shorten to 5 minutes for enterprise customers at a slight price premium or with a larger commit.

3) Discount bands for 12-month commits with burst add-on
- 25% commit (e.g., you reserve 25% of expected steady-state on Dedicated): baseline pricing, no additional discount on surge tokens.
- 50% commit: 10% discount on monthly commit fee; surge-per-token premium reduced by 15%.
- 75%+ commit: 18% discount on monthly commit; surge token premium reduced by 30% and cooldown reduces to 10 minutes.

I attached: "Redwood-Dedicated-Burst-Addendum-v1.pdf" which is draft language we usually add to Dedicated contracts. For your file, we modeled three scenarios (low/med/high burst) using the numbers from your spreadsheet.

Next steps: review the addendum, we'll iterate on cooldown and activation fees to match your usage pattern. If you want to lock a larger discount (e.g., 22% on commit), we can do that in exchange for a 24-month commit or a higher initial commit payment.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales — Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarification on burst pricing + cooldown for Dedicated GPU pool

Quick engineering note (copied for transparency):

- Surge cost drivers: short spikes (sub-6s token bursts) are expensive because of context switch and scheduling; longer sustained bursts amortize better. For Acme's profile (many short interactive queries + intermittent long batch inferences), the recommended approach is to size GPU pool for the 95th percentile steady-state and lean on burst for short tails.
- GPU sizing suggestion: based on your spreadsheet, a 16-GPU pool (A100 equiv) with a 50% commit gives predictable latency at your 95th p99 target and keeps expected monthly surge spend under ~18% of the commit cost in the medium scenario.

If we move to 75% commit and add the shorter cooldown, you'll see surge spend drop materially because the system will rely less on burst to smooth spikes.

Connor, can you confirm whether the activation fee applies when burst capacity is served from already-warm pre-provisioned nodes (we offered warm warm standbys for enterprise previously)?

-Karthik

From: connor_obrien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Laura Jensen <procurement@acme-bio.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on burst pricing + cooldown for Dedicated GPU pool

Karthik — yes, activation fee is waived when surge capacity is fulfilled from warm standbys that are pre-provisioned and pinned for your account. There is a separate line item for the warm-standby reservation (monthly), but it removes the per-activation charge and improves cold-start latency.

For Acme's traffic: if you want minimal tail latency on interactive queries, the warm-standby + 50% commit is the best balance. I'll add projected cost delta in a follow-up if the team requests it.

-Connor
